name: LinkedGrow
tagline: AI tool for drafting, scheduling and growing a LinkedIn presence.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The writing half of this is a solved problem: an LLM with a few good prompts and a library of hook patterns will draft LinkedIn posts as well as any wrapper around the same models. The part that does not survive a one-shot build is LinkedIn itself, which has no useful public API for posting or commenting on a personal profile, so any real automation means browser extensions or headless sessions and a nonzero chance of getting your account limited. You can build a very good local drafting studio, idea inbox and posting queue in a weekend, then paste manually. You will not get engagement analytics, comment automation, or reliable scheduled publishing without either an extension you also have to build or an official partner integration you cannot get.
coreLoopDIY: A local app that turns rough notes into LinkedIn post drafts using an LLM, keeps a hook and format library, and holds a dated queue you copy from and paste by hand.
requirements: Node 20 and a local SQLite file
Manual copy and paste into LinkedIn, or your own browser extension if you accept the ban risk
whatYouLose: Actual scheduled publishing, since LinkedIn does not hand out personal posting access
Engagement analytics pulled back from LinkedIn: impressions, follower deltas, which hook worked
Comment and DM automation, which is the part most growth tools actually sell
A mobile surface for capturing ideas and approving drafts on the train
Whatever aggregate signal the vendor has about which post shapes are currently performing
moatNotes: The moat is platform access, not intelligence. LinkedIn's hostility to automation is the product's main asset and its main risk.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the annoying part is not writing the post, it is getting it onto LinkedIn on a schedule and seeing whether it worked. People pay someone else to maintain the fragile extension, absorb the API and detection whack-a-mole, and hand them a dashboard that says impressions went up. A local drafting tool covers the creative loop honestly and leaves the last mile to your thumbs, which is fine for one person and useless for anyone managing five profiles.
notes: Build the drafting studio, keep the manual paste, and stop pretending the analytics tab was ever the reason you posted.
prompt:
Build a local-only LinkedIn post studio. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Node 20, TypeScript, Next.js App Router, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Tailwind. Single repo, runs with `npm run dev` on localhost. LLM calls go to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint using OPENAI_API_KEY from .env.local. Never commit .env.local; ship .env.example.

Data model in SQLite:
- ideas: id, raw_text, source_url, created_at, status (raw | drafted | archived)
- drafts: id, idea_id, body, hook_id, variant_index, created_at, chosen (bool)
- hooks: id, label, pattern_text, notes (seed with 12 common LinkedIn opener patterns, e.g. contrarian claim, numbered list, short story, before/after)
- queue: id, draft_id, slot_date, slot_time, posted_at (nullable), post_url (nullable)

Screens:
1. Inbox: one textarea to dump a raw idea, list of raw ideas, button "Draft".
2. Draft view: calls the LLM once and returns 3 variants for the selected idea, each using a different hook pattern from the hooks table. Show them side by side, editable in place, save edits back to drafts. Enforce a visible character counter with a warning past 1300 characters (LinkedIn's see-more fold at roughly 200 characters should be marked with a line in the editor).
3. Queue: a simple week grid. Drag or assign a chosen draft to a date and time slot. Each queued item has a big "Copy" button that puts the final text on the clipboard and a checkbox to mark it posted, plus an optional field to paste the resulting post URL.
4. Library: list and edit hook patterns, and a plain list of your posted history with the URLs you pasted.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt: LinkedIn API calls, browser automation, cookie or session scraping, comment or DM automation, impression scraping, multi-user support, notifications. Publishing is manual by design; say so in the README.

System prompt for drafting must instruct: no hashtag spam, maximum one emoji, no "I'm humbled to announce", short lines, one concrete detail per paragraph, and end with a question only if it is not rhetorical filler.

Deliverables: working app, seeded hooks, README with setup in five lines or fewer, and `npm run export` that dumps all posts and queue to a single markdown file.
